So for processingInstruction true: "<!xml!>" . For false: "<?xml?>". That's weird but follow.

When attributes added, they will be added after a space. So getWholeDeclaration returns string of attributes (with preceding spaces). OuterHtmlHead includes them.

That's public method getWholeDeclaration() returns whole declaration string (but note it constructs only attributes? Wait getWholeDeclaration() builds sb, then getWholeDeclaration(sb, new Document.OutputSettings()); returns sb.toString().trim(); So output is only attribute part? Actually it doesn't include leading <? etc. So getWholeDeclaration returns string of attributes (prefixed spaces then attributes). Let's test that.

Thus test: XmlDeclaration decl = new XmlDeclaration("xml", false); decl.attr("version","1.0"); decl.attr("encoding","utf-8"); String whole = decl.getWholeDeclaration(); Expect " version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"" trimmed? Actually trim removes leading/trailing whitespace, so leading space removed, resulting "version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"". So assert that.

Edge case: no attributes returns empty string.

Test outerHtmlHead: capture output via StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); decl.outerHtmlHead(sb, 0, new Document.OutputSettings()); Then sb.toString() should be "<!xml!>" for processing instruction without attributes.

When attributes present, include space and attribute html. For attribute html format: attribute.html(accum,out) writes key="value". So expected: "<!xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"!>"? Wait order: after coreValue, getWholeDeclaration adds space then attribute html. Then after that, outerHtmlHead appends isProcessingInstruction ? "!" : "?" then ">" . So final: "<!xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"!>" (note space before version). Need to verify attribute order: attributes() returns list insertion order; we add version then encoding.

Test toString returns same as outerHtml() - need to call toString and compare.

Will need to import org.junit.* and static org.junit.Assert.*.

Also test that outerHtmlTail does nothing (no exception). Could call method and ensure no changes.
